subject: Fathom Analytics production outage — head-of-line stalls & KV config request
messages:
From: Ava Miller <ava@fathomanalytics.com>

Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@fathomanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency & 5xx spike — started 12:05 PDT

Hi Neha,

We're hitting a production problem this morning. Around 12:05 PDT our P95 latency spiked from ~420ms to ~2.8s and we started seeing a sustained 5xx rate of about 1.2%. The spike correlates with a jump in small, single-turn requests to one of our high-concurrency routes (session_id prefix A1*). We've attached a short perf snapshot and a heapdump.

This is impacting our user-facing inference flows (real-time transcripts). Can your team confirm if anything changed on the Redwood side? Any immediate mitigations we can try? We're on a tight SLA and need an ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Ava
SRE Lead, Fathom Analytics

Attachments: perf-snapshot-20270515.json, heapdump-20270515.txt

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency & 5xx spike — triage notes

Quick triage notes from infra:
- Observed pattern: single-turn, low-token requests from a hot key-prefix (A1*) are creating many tiny batches. This causes head-of-line (HOL) stalls on the shared batch lanes — long-lived KV cache misses are stalling subsequent requests for the same lane.
- Root cause hypothesis: a recent prefix eviction policy change (reduce per-prefix TTL to improve memory churn) + increased small-request fanout from the customer's app created rapid prefix thrash. The runtime is evicting and reloading KV cache entries aggressively, which spikes latency and 500s when hot prefixes contend.
- Evidence: attached perf snapshot shows a rise in cache-eviction events, KV fill latency, and concurrent small-batch queue depth. Heapdump shows increased active cache churn.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (no binary change):
1) Increase per-prefix cache TTL for customer prefix A1* to 45s (from 5s) and raise max-prefix entries for their tenant shard (quick config flip).
2) Batching tweak: allow small single-request batches to be forwarded on a separate "fast lane" (reduce HOL impact) by enabling fast-lane flag for tenant.
3) Temporarily pin a lightweight, lower-precision model variant for prefixes with spike to reduce token-generation time.

I can push (1) and (2) in the next 12 minutes. Expected effect: P95 should return closer to baseline within 2–5 minutes after config change; 5xx should drop. We'll monitor and be ready to rollback.

Attaching: perf-snapshot-20270515.json.

-Vivek
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Miller <ava@fathomanalytics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Production latency & 5xx spike — proposed mitigation

Ava — thanks for the quick report. We can implement the config changes Vivek suggested. Before we proceed, could you confirm:
1) Do you approve Redwood flipping the per-prefix TTL and enabling fast-lane batching for prefix A1*?
2) Is it OK if we temporarily route A1* requests to the lower-precision variant for up to 30 minutes as a test?

If you approve, we'll make the change and monitor carefully. We'll also provide a short communication to your ops team with the observed impact and a recommended long-term fix (prefix awareness and client-level batching).

For reference, Fathom wrote earlier in thread: 

> This is impacting our user-facing inference flows (real-time transcripts). We're on a tight SLA and need an ETA for mitigation.

Neha — I'll coordinate comms. Vivek, stand by to roll this in once Ava confirms.

-Marissa
